task.title: WKWebView claims anchor support the popover CSS path can't actually use
task.description:
Maintainer retest (2026-08-16, .app built 16:23 — POST-#163): the Adding-to and Move-to popovers still don't render usably in the mac app. Since #163's JS fallback demonstrably works when it runs (forced-fallback probe, pixel-exact), the prime suspect is DETECTION: anchor_positioning_supported() likely returns true on this macOS's WKWebView (Safari-family WebKit added CSS Anchor Positioning in 26.0), so the CSS anchor path is taken — and some feature it relies on misbehaves there: candidates are position-area on top-layer popovers, the @position-try(flip-block) blocks (note: those appear embedded in inline style strings in popover.rs — verify how they're actually applied and whether ANY engine honors them from there), anchor() with implicit anchors, or WKWebView-specific top-layer anchor bugs.

Required first step — REAL-ENGINE ground truth, not simulation: get a JS/CSS probe running inside actual WKWebView on this Mac. Viable harnesses: (a) a tiny swiftc-compiled WKWebView harness loading a probe page and printing CSS.supports() results plus a LIVE MEASUREMENT of an anchored test popover (does anchor()/position-area actually move it); (b) a debug tauri build with inspectable webview driven however automatable. Establish exactly which declarations work and which don't.

Then fix accordingly, smallest honest change: make detection feature-exact (probe the SPECIFIC capabilities the CSS path needs — a runtime one-shot measurement probe beats CSS.supports string checks if the engine parses-but-misbehaves) so WKWebView takes the #163 fallback; OR fix the CSS path's declarations if the engine supports a correct variant. Either way the maintainer's rebuilt .app must show working tray Move-to and catalog Adding-to pickers. Prior art: #148 (anchor path), #163 (fallback + forced probe), design/component-gap-analysis.md's WKWebView caveat. References the closed WB-01M05K42G96ZSGHEBHKQ47CBDV (do not reopen it — this is the successor with new evidence).
